chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him); and Yazeed ibn Hammad and others, from Abu Jameela, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There is no one except that he has a share in adultery; so the adultery of the two eyes is the look, and the adultery of the mouth is the kiss, and the adultery of the two hands is the touch, whether the private part confirms it or denies it.
ai.seo_question: What are the different types of adultery mentioned in Shia hadith regarding the senses?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the concept of 'zina of the limbs,' a key theme in Shia ethics where sensory inputs are viewed as precursors to physical acts. It establishes a holistic view of chastity, linking the gaze, kiss, and touch to the confirmation of the private part, thereby emphasizing that moral integrity begins with the senses before manifesting in action.
